title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Desk Guide: Earnings Disregard Share for Claimants with a Definite Recall Date
content:
For a weekly payment on Unemployment Benefit Claims, the disregard share — the share of the weekly benefit amount that sets the week's earnings disregard, rounded to the cent — follows the definite recall date recorded on the claim and whether the week reports earnings (gross earnings above zero on the week's certification).

| Definite recall date on the claim | Week reports earnings | Disregard share |
|---|---|---|
| On or after the handling date and no more than 240 days after it | Yes | 0.4 (the near-recall share) |
| More than 240 days after the handling date | Yes | 0.35 (the far-recall share) |
| None, a date already passed, or any recall date with no earnings in the week | — | The program's disregard share |

Any other weekly payment uses the program's disregard share.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical, earnings reported)

| Recall date | Share |
|---|---|
| 240 days after the handling date | 0.4 |
| 241 days after the handling date | 0.35 |
| No recall date recorded | The program's disregard share |

For a weekly benefit amount of 346.00, the 0.4 share gives a disregard of 138.40 and the 0.35 share 121.10.
